name: Russia
hook: Czars, a revolution and Siberia: the Russia clues keep asking about the same rulers and winter.

facts.label: Catherine the Great
facts.statement: Catherine the Great, born Sophie, took the throne in 1762 after a palace coup led by Grigory Orlov and later ordered exploration of Alaska.

facts.label: Peter the Great
facts.statement: Peter the Great opened Russia to the West and built St. Petersburg, including a palace called the Russian Versailles; the Bronze Horseman celebrates him.

facts.label: Ivan the Terrible
facts.statement: Ivan the Terrible, Russia's first czar, conquered much of Siberia and in 1565 won the right to execute traitors at will.

facts.label: Siberia
facts.statement: Siberia, basically all of Russia east of the Urals, may take its name from a Tatar word meaning "sleeping land" and was long a place of exile.

facts.label: Vladimir Lenin
facts.statement: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolsheviks, whose speeches inspired the Russian Revolution; a series of strokes left him unable to speak.

facts.label: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
facts.statement: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky turned Pushkin's Eugene Onegin into an opera and wrote the music for Balanchine's Theme and Variations.

facts.label: the largest country
facts.statement: Russia is the world's largest country by area, and the Moscow Canal links its capital to the Volga.
